summary: Listed as still standing near Chapleau, Ontario, with its cupola removed and now a communications tower; a 2013 note says the MNR has decided to remove many such towers.

facts.status_note: Listed as still standing with its cupola removed; a note on the list says that, as of 2013, the MNR has decided to remove many such towers.

access.note: The list says the MNR no longer maintains these towers, has removed the bottom 6.1 m (20 ft) of ladder, and asks visitors not to climb.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both copies of the same still-standing list. The GeoCities copy gives no date for the list; the forestrangers copy has a note dated as of 2013 that the MNR has decided to remove many of these towers, so standing status today is unconfirmed. Firelookout.ca has no Alcorn record in our cache. The Ontario LIO fire-tower layer (data/raw/ontario_lio/fire_towers.geojson) has 'Alcorn' (OBJECTID 599, TOWER_IDENT TOW-34533-1, verified, location within 10 m at 48.13756, -83.05378), but it has no build date, height, district or condition, and it cannot be cited: the GeoHub dataset page returns 13 characters and the GeoJSON has no fetchable source URL, so the story leaves it out. No build date, height, design, staffing or Alcorn-specific access rule was found. The restricted access level is inferred from the list's general no-climb note, not from an Alcorn-specific rule. The Ontario Parks page for Chapleau-Nemegosenda River Provincial Park does not mention a tower. The story is short because the evidence is thin.
